headline: Manus, an AI agent startup that began in China, has raised more than $500 million in its first funding round since Beijing blocked Meta's deal to buy it.
score_reason: Pool score 7 kept: the company announced the round and several outlets carry it; the undisclosed valuation is noted, not scored down.
importance_line: It shows investors still back Manus as an independent company after the Meta deal was blocked, but the valuation is undisclosed and the company must still prove scale, profit and regulatory fit.
summary: Reuters reports that Manus raised more than $500 million, led by Boyu Capital and IDG Capital, with existing backers Tencent, HSG and ZhenFund also investing. Han Lin, China country director at The Asia Group, says the company's immediate task is “proving scale, profitability and regulatory alignment.”
notes: Reuters blocked here (401). Facts read in the Lavx.hu, TokenPost and Streamlinefeed copies, which do not name Reuters; the Reuters credit rests on the Reuters headline in Google News and the chunk. Link is the Reuters link from the chunk (not opened here). Score 7 kept.
